title: EGY-09 · Practical problems: pharmacy, telephone, home, office

blocks.text: EGY-09 · Practical problems: pharmacy, telephone, home, office
Lesson overview

Luca is in Cairo for the summer course and lives again in the palace of ʿAmm Aḥmad, the goalkeeper who knows from the previous summer: ʿAmm Aḥmad Found him a small furnished apartment on the fourth floor. The days are full of lessons and discoveries, but also of small problems: a cold, bad air conditioning, internet that does not go, a line in an office, a wrong order. In this unit you learn to explain a malaise in the pharmacy, buy a SIM card and an internet package, ask for a repair, get away with it in an office and complain politely, in Egyptian. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-22, B1-23 and INT-01.

rows: 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 143–148), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian conversation partner
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. tell how you are and describe common symptoms (headache, sore throat, fever, cold) and understand the
indications of the pharmacist;
2. buy a SIM card, reload credit, choose an internet package, report that the network is not working;
3. report a failure in the home and request a repair;
4. orient yourself in an office: the row, the form, the door, the return tomorrow;
5. Crying nicely but firmly, and accepting the apology.
Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).
1. Dialogue 1 · At the pharmacy
Dokki, in the evening. Luca walks into a pharmacy under the house.

rows: Your pharmacist: Good evening, would you like?
⁧مساء النور. عندي برد من امبارح،⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩ ⁧وزوري بيوجعني أوي.⁩
Lūka: masāʾ in-nūr. ʿandi bard min imbāriḥ, wi-zōri biywgaʿni ʾawi.
Good evening. I've had a cold since yesterday and my throat hurts.
The pharmacist: Do you have a fever?
⁧لأ، مش أوي. بس عندي صداع، ومش⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩ ⁧قادر أنام كويس.⁩
Lūka: laʾ, miš ʾawi. bass ʿandi ṣudāʿ, wi- miš ʾādir anām kwayyis.
No, not so much. But I have a headache and I can't sleep well.
The pharmacist: Have you been very in the sun?
⁧أيوه، امبارح كنت في الأهرامات طول⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩ ⁧وبعدين ركبت المترو والتكييف⁩ … ⁧اليوم⁩ ⁧كان ساقع جدًا.⁩
Lūka: aywa, imbāriḥ kunt fi l-ahramāt ṭūl il-yōm… wi-baʿdēn rikibt il-metro wi-t-takyīf kān sāʾiʿ giddan.
Luca: Yes, yesterday I was in the pyramids all day... and then I took the subway and the air conditioning was freezing.
⁧ده بيحصل لأجانب كتير في⁩ : ⁧الصيدلي⁩ ⁧الصيف: حر برا، وتكييف ساقع جوا!⁩
iṣ-ṣaydali: da biyḥṣal li-agānib kitīr fi ṣ-ṣēf: ḥarr barra, wi-takyīf sāʾiʿ guwwa!
The pharmacist: It happens to many foreigners in the summer: hot outside and air conditioning cold inside!
All right, what do I do?
⁧هديك أقراص للزور ومسكن⁩ : ⁧الصيدلي⁩ ⁧للصداع. خدهم زي ما مكتوب على العلبة.⁩ ⁧واشرب مية كتير وحاجات سخنة.⁩
iṣ-ṣaydali: hadīk aʾrāṣ li-z-zōr wi- musakkin li-ṣ-ṣudāʿ. ḫudhum zayy ma maktūb ʿala l-ʿilba. w-išrab mayya ktīr wi-ḥagāt suḫna.
Your pharmacist: I'll give you some throat pills and an analgesic for a headache. Take it as it is written on the package. And drink lots of water and hot stuff.
⁧لأ، دول من غير روشتة. بس لو⁩ : ⁧الصيدلي⁩ ⁧السخونية زادت أو الكحة فضلت أكتر من⁩ ⁧تلات أيام، لازم تروح لدكتور.⁩
iṣ-ṣaydali: laʾ, dōl min ġēr rušetta. bass law is-suḫuniyya zādit aw il-kuḥḥa fiḍlit aktar min talat ayyām, lāzim tirūḥ li-duktūr.
The pharmacist: No, these are no prescription. But if the fever rises or the cough lasts longer than three days, you should go to a doctor.
iṣ-ṣaydali: itfaḍḍal il-fatūra. alf salāma ʿalēk!
The pharmacist: Here's the receipt. Heal soon!

I have a headache. ʿandi. zōri biywgaʿni My throat hurts.wagaʿ · yiwgaʿ "do evil": subject the part of the body, object the person). suḫuniyya From sōḫn "warm" is the word. miš ʾādir anām I cannot sleep.ʾādirParticiple of ʾidir, EGY-05). ḥarr bar, takyīf sāʾiʿ guwwa: sāʾiʿ (EGY-)08 bārid). zayy ma maktūb ʿala l-ʿilba • as written on the package: for doses, always follow the leaflet or your doctor. rušetta (from English). fiḍlit It has remained, continued. alf salāma ʿalēk! "A thousand wishes for healing" , reply allāh Yisallimak.
2. Being sick: Egyptian and fuṣḥā
⁧سَلَامَتُكَ⁩ · ⁧شَفَاكَ اللهُ⁩ alf salāma ʿalēk · salamtak heal soon

The body part + biywgaʿni. In Egyptian it is said that the part of the body hurts me: rāsi btiwgaʿni My head hurts, my head hurts.rās is female), baṭni btiwgaʿni My belly hurts, ḍahri biywgaʿni My back hurts. sināni btiwgaʿni I'm sick of a tooth.
3. At the pharmacy

rows: Do you have anything for the cold?
I'd like an analgesic for a headache.

blocks.text: The forms of drugs. ʾurṣ (pl. aʾrāṣ) Composed of tablets, pills and pills ḥabbāya (pl. ḥubūb) • Pill šarāb "Syruppo" · marham "pomata" · ʾaṭra Droplets (Lett. "Drop" means a drop in the water. Practical advice. In Egypt the pharmacist is often the first one to be addressed for minor problems, and many pharmacies deliver at home; for any doubts about dosage or a missed symptom, the right person is your doctor.
4. The phone and internet
⁧عايز خط جديد⁩ ʿāyiz ḫaṭṭ gdīd I would like a new SIM (line)

rows: I'd like to reload the credit
Is there a monthly internet package?
Internet is not working · There is no internet

blocks.text: ⁧مش سامعك كويس، الخط بيقطع⁩ miš samʿak kwayyis, il-ḫaṭṭ biyʾaṭṭaʿ I can't hear you well, the line goes and comes.

ḫaṭṭ The following points are inserted after the entry into force of this Regulation: SIM-SIM · šaḥan · yišḥan Recharge, reload, reload, reload. bāʾa Package wāʾiʿ In-nett wāʾiʿ The internet is down. · ḫilṣ It's finished. biyʾaṭṭaʿ It's off. To buy a SIM card you usually need an ID (the passport, for foreigners): the store registers the line in your name.
5. Problems in the Home

rows: Can you send me a plumber · an electrician · a technician?

blocks.text: ⁧هيصلحه إمتى؟⁩ hayṣallaḥu Imta? When do you fix it?
ʿaṭlān and šaġġāl. ʿaṭlān (EGY-)06) e šaġġāl The two keywords are working: il-asansēr šaġġāl in-naharda maʾṭūʿ "Switched" is used for water, light, road.
6. Dialogue 2 · Call ʿAmm Aḥmad
The next day, Luca calls the doorman.

rows: ⁧ألو، عم أحمد؟ أنا لوكا، من الشقة اللي⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩ ⁧في الدور الرابع.⁩
Lūka: alō, ʿAmm Aḥmad? ana Lūka, mi š-šaʾʾa lli fi d-dōr ir-rābiʿ.
Hello. ʿAmm Aḥmad? I'm Luca from the fourth floor apartment.
⁧عم أحمد: أهلًا يا أستاذ لوكا! خير؟⁩
ʿAmm Aḥmad: ahlan ya ustāz Lūka! ḫēr?
ʿAmm AḥmadGood morning, Mr. Luca! What's going on?
Lūka: it-takyīf ʿaṭlān mi-ṣ-ṣubḥ, wi-l- ʾōḍa ḥarr giddan.
The air conditioning has been broken since this morning, and in the room it is a terrible heat.
⁧عم أحمد: يا خبر! ولا يهمك، هكلم الفني⁩ ⁧ييجي يشوفه.⁩
ʿAmm Aḥmad: ya ḫabar! wala yhimmak, hakallim il-fanni yīgi yšufu.
ʿAmm Aḥmad- Damn it! Don't worry, I'll call the tech to see her.
⁧عم أحمد: النهارده بعد العصر، إن شاء الله.⁩
ʿAmm Aḥmad: in-naharda baʿd il-ʿaṣr, in šāʾ allāh.
ʿAmm AḥmadToday, in the late afternoon, if God wills.
Lūka: «in šāʾ allāh» in-naharda… walla «in šāʾ allāh» bukra?
Luke: "If God wills" today... or "if God wants" tomorrow?
⁧عم أحمد: لا يا سيدي، النهارده! أنا بنفسي⁩ ⁧هطلع معاه. حاجة تانية؟⁩
ʿAmm Aḥmad: laʾ ya sīdi, in-naharda! ana bi-nafsi haṭlaʿ maʿāh. ḥāga tanya?
ʿAmm Aḥmad: No, sir, today! I'll go up with him myself. Anything else?
⁧آه، والنت كمان واقع. والمية السخنة⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩ ⁧مش بتيجي في الحمام.⁩
Lūka: āh, wi-n-nett kamān wāʾiʿ. wi-l- mayya s-suḫna miš bitīgi fi l-ḥammām.
Oh, the Internet isn't working. And the bathroom doesn't get hot water.
⁧عم أحمد: النت ده مش شغلي، لازم تكلم⁩ ⁧الشركة. والسخان، الفني يشوفه برضه.⁩
ʿAmm Aḥmad: in-nett da miš šuġli, lāzim tkallim iš-šerka. wi-s-saḫḫān, il- fanni yšufu barḍu.
ʿAmm Aḥmad: The Internet is not my business, you have to call the company. The water heater looks at him too.
⁧متشكر أوي يا عم أحمد. تعبتك معايا!⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩
Lūka: mutašakkir ʾawi ya ʿAmm Aḥmad. taʿabtak maʿāya!
Luca: Thank you very much, ʿAmm Aḥmad. I gave you a big trouble!
⁧عم أحمد: تعب إيه يا راجل! إنت زي ابني.⁩ ⁧ولما الفني ييجي، ما تدفعلوش غير لما⁩ ⁧يخلص الشغل.⁩
ʿAmm Aḥmad: taʿab ēh ya rāgil! inta zayy ibni. wi-lamma l-fanni yīgi, ma- tidfaʿlūš ġēr lamma yḫallaṣ iš-šuġl.
ʿAmm Aḥmad: What a disturbance! You're like a son. And when the tech comes, don't pay him until he's done his job.

7. In an office

rows: Where's the line? · Who is the last?
Where do I get the number?
Need a photocopy of your passport

blocks.text: Patience and courtesy. In the Egyptian offices he often expects, and thetaʿāla bukra... is not uncommon. The calm, the smile and the formulas work better: law samaḥt, ya fandom (to an employee), maʿlišš, kattar ḫērak Thank you very much (Lett. God multiply your good.
8. Begin nicely.

rows: I've been waiting for an hour.
Accept the apology: "No matter" - no problem

blocks.text: Answer the apology. Egyptian ʾasfīn ʾawi We're really sorry. You answer wala yhimmak or ḥaṣal ḫēr It went well as it did: the complaint closes with cordiality.
9. Pronunciation

The emphasis in the words of health. ṣudāʿ, ṣaydaliyya, ḍarbit šams, ḍahri: The vowel close to the empathetic consonant is darker. Repeat with the tutor the minimum pairs: ṣēf • Summer • sēf Swords ṭīn Mud (mud) / tīn . The qāf disappears: ʾ. ʾurṣ (fuṣḥā ⁧قُرْص⁩ ), maʾṭūʿ "Sintered" ( ⁧مَقْطُوع⁩ ), wāʾiʿ "Caded" ( ⁧وَاقِع⁩ ), maʿʾūl Religious ( ⁧مَعْقُول⁩ ).

Call (in writing) to the doorman: presented, explains that the light is missing in the kitchen and that the bathroom faucet drips, ask when a technician can come, thanks.

12. Listening
Egyptian scripts should be read by an Egyptian speaker (tutor, tandem partner): vocal synthesis does not pronounce the dialect reliably.
Script A · Dialogues 1 and 2
The reader reads the dialogues at normal speed. Listen without reading, then answer questions a) and b) for the year 8.

13. Oral production
1. In pharmacy (session). Roleplay with the pharmacist tutor: describe two symptoms, respond to his
questions, ask how to take the product and if you need the recipe.
2. The phone store. Roleplay: Buy a SIM with internet, ask for package prices and return the
day after because the internet doesn't work.
3. The office. Role-playing game: you've been in line for an hour, the clerk says the system is locked and back tomorrow.
You complain nicely, ask for the manager, find a solution.

blocks.text: 16. Unit verification

Twenty points; Exceeding at least 16. Parts A and B are made by voice with the tutor, who marks points; Without tutors, write in transliteration. A · Health and pharmacy (6 points). 1. My head hurts. · 2. I've had a cough for three days. · 3. Do you have anything for the cold? · 4. How do I take it before or after meals? · 5. Do you need a prescription? · 6. Heal soon! (and reply) B · House, telephone, offices (8 points). 7. The water heater's not working. · 8. There's no light in the kitchen. · 9. When's the tech coming? · 10. I'd like a SIM card with an internet package. · 11. The credit is over. · 12. Where's the line? Who's the last one? · 13. I've been waiting an hour! · 14. Can I speak to the person in charge? C · Understand (6 points). Translate into English: 15. in-nett wāʾiʿ min imbāriḥ. · 16. is-sīstim wāʾiʿ, taʿāla Bukra. · 17. ma fi īdi ḥāga. · 18. ʾasfīn ʾawi, hanibʿatlak il-ṭalab ḥālan. · 19. taʿabtak maʿāya. · 20. kattar ḫērak!
17. To switch to the next unit

Switch to EGY-10 if you have at least 16/20 and if in the three role-playing games you have solved the problem without going to fuṣḥā and without losing the courtesy. In EGY-10, the last unit of the track, express opinions, talk about Egyptian TV series and movies and start listening to the authentic Egyptian.
